applicationPool.reason: GTK4 plus libadwaita end-user application (meson.build: dependency('gtk4')), builds and runs offline, persists only GSettings and its own history file under the profile. Currency conversion is the one network flow and is not on any selected trigger path. candidateDefects counts merged MRs in the most recent 100 whose description closes or fixes a numbered issue

GTK4 plus GtkSourceView plus libadwaita application (meson.build: dependency('gtk4', version: gtk_req)), fully offline, writes only to files the operator opens plus its own session state. candidateDefects counts merged MRs in the most recent 100 whose description closes or fixes a numbered issue

GTK4 plus libadwaita Vala application (meson.build: dependency('gtk4')), the world clock database ships with libgweather locally so the add-clock flow needs no network, and state lives in GSettings only. candidateDefects counts merged MRs in the most recent 100 whose description closes or fixes a numbered issue

Rust GTK4 plus libadwaita drawing application (meson.build declares dependency('gtk4') for the ui subproject, crates/rnote-ui/Cargo.toml pulls gtk4 and adw), runs entirely offline and writes only the notebook files the operator chooses. Its canvas is a custom GTK widget driven by GtkGesture and GtkEventController, which is exactly the adapter surface under test. candidateDefects is the GitHub search count of merged pull requests linked to an issue
small GTK4 plus libadwaita application (meson.build: dependency('gtk4', version: '>=4.6')), no network, no state outside its own recent-characters GSettings key. Not yet mined for defects

GTK4 plus libadwaita application (meson.build: dependency('gtk4', version: gtk_req_version)), reads the font tree read-only and installs fonts only into the user's own ~/.local/share/fonts. Not yet mined for defects

PyGObject GTK4 modelling application (pyproject.toml requires PyGObject, classifier 'Environment :: X11 Applications :: GTK'), offline, saves only to the model file the operator picks. Adds a Python binding flavour of the GTK adapter next to the C, Vala, and Rust ones. Not yet mined for defects

GTK4 plus libadwaita application (meson.build: dependency('gtk4', version: '>=4.15.1')) and read-only in normal use, but it also offers a delete-to-trash action and by default scans the whole home directory. Only admissible if the trigger is pinned to a scratch directory and the trash action is never on the path

GTK4 plus libadwaita application (meson.build: dependency('gtk4', version: '>= 4.21.2')) but it stores nothing itself: every read and write goes through evolution-data-server D-Bus services that must be started and torn down inside the container, and any account backend would reach the network. Admissible only with a private session bus and a local-only calendar source
the file manager's core flows copy, move, rename, trash, and delete files anywhere the user can reach, so the trigger mutates state outside the application's own profile by construction
writes system and session configuration (users, network, printers, power) through privileged D-Bus services; the trigger is not non-destructive and needs a live system bus
partitions, formats, and mounts block devices via udisks2; destructive against host state and unrunnable in an unprivileged container
requires PackageKit or Flatpak plus remote repositories for every meaningful flow; installs and removes system packages, so it is both network-bound and destructive
map tiles, geocoding, and routing all come from third-party services; there is no offline trigger
Matrix client: every user-visible flow requires a homeserver, which is a third-party service the campaign cannot stand up under --network none
the GTK client is a BitTorrent front end; core flows need peers and trackers on the network and write downloads outside the profile
the toolkit under test, not an application built on it. Its own test suite would measure GTK rather than the ReproIt GTK adapter
IDE platform with plugin, container, and language-server subsystems; framework-scale rather than an end-user application, and its flows spawn external toolchains

selectedDefects.issueTitle: Orca doesn't announce the "Search" and "Replace" text fields
selectedDefects.whySuitable: the defect exists only in the accessibility projection of the widget tree, which is the GTK adapter's primary observation channel. The search bar's inner GtkText carries no accessible-role and the replace entry carries no accessible label, so on the affected revision the AT-SPI tree exposes the search field with a generic role and the replace field with an empty name. The fix sets accessible-role=text-box on the GtkText and an accessible label on the replace entry. Observable: open the search bar with Ctrl+F and read the role and name of the two entry objects from the AT-SPI tree. No pixels, no timing, and nothing outside the widget hierarchy the adapter already walks

selectedDefects.issueTitle: "Document Type" window is not closable with ESC key
selectedDefects.whySuitable: a key must be delivered to a real GTK widget and its effect read back from window state, so the trigger crosses the adapter's key-injection path rather than any internal API. Escape pressed inside the dialog's GtkSearchEntry emits stop-search; on the affected revision nothing is connected to that signal and the AdwDialog stays mapped, on the fixed revision the handler calls adw_dialog_close. Observable: after opening the Document Type dialog and sending Escape, does an object with that dialog's accessible name still exist in the AT-SPI tree. This pairs with the accessibility defect above by exercising the action half of the adapter against the same application

selectedDefects.issueTitle: Cursor disappears when click on history
selectedDefects.whySuitable: a pointer click must be delivered at real coordinates inside a GtkListBoxRow and the consequence read as a focus transition, which is exactly the click-plus-focus pair the GTK adapter has to get right. The history row is a ListBoxRow with focus-on-click left at its GTK default of true on the affected revision, so clicking a history item moves keyboard focus off the equation GtkSourceView and the caret disappears. The fix adds focus-on-click: false in history-entry.blp. Observable: which object holds the AT-SPI focused state after the click, and whether subsequently typed digits still reach the equation display

selectedDefects.issueTitle: Default keyboard focus is on the Cancel button when adding a clock
selectedDefects.whySuitable: initial focus placement is a property of the GTK widget tree at map time, so the adapter must observe the accessibility state of a freshly created window rather than react to an input it sent. On the affected revision the AdwDialog has no focus-widget property and GTK gives initial focus to the Cancel button, so text typed straight after opening the dialog goes nowhere. The fix sets focus-widget=location_entry in world-location-dialog.ui. Observable: which object reports the AT-SPI focused state immediately after the dialog is mapped, and whether typed characters land in the location GtkEntry. A third application, and a different failure shape from the other three: no user action at all is required to expose it

selectedDefects.issueTitle: Zooming with ctrl + scroll does not work when caps lock is on
selectedDefects.whySuitable: the defect is in how the application reads GdkModifierType off a GTK event controller, so it can only be reproduced by delivering a real scroll event with a real modifier state through GTK. canvaswrapper.rs compared the controller's modifier state to ControlMask with strict equality, so with Caps Lock latched the state is Control plus Lock and the zoom branch never runs; the fix switches to .contains. Observable: the canvas zoom factor shown in the zoom control before and after a Ctrl+scroll with the lock modifier set. This is the only selected candidate whose trigger requires modifier state rather than a plain key or click, which is the part of the GTK adapter nothing else here covers, and it is the only Rust binding in the set

blockers.detail: None of the ten revisions named in selectedDefects has been built or run. This record qualifies candidates from repository, issue, and merge-request data plus git object verification only; every entry carries qualification 'selected-not-executed'. Docker was deliberately not used during this gate. buildQualified therefore has no value for any pool entry, unlike the electron-linux record which was written after its campaigns

Four of the five selected defects are observed through AT-SPI (accessible role, accessible name, focused state). The GTK adapter's ability to read the AT-SPI tree of an application running under Xvfb with at-spi2-core on a private session bus has not been demonstrated in this repository yet. If that channel does not work, gnome-text-editor-search-entry-a11y-771 is unobservable entirely and the three focus-based candidates fall back to weaker text-content assertions

rnote-ctrl-scroll-capslock-1617 needs a scroll event delivered while the Lock modifier is latched. Whether the harness can latch Caps Lock and have GTK report it in the controller's GdkModifierType under Xvfb is untested. If it cannot, this candidate is not reproducible and the set drops to four

Two otherwise strong candidates were dropped for lack of a referenced issue, which the gate requires: gnome-calculator MR 438 'Fix keyboard shortcut for preferences not working' (ff2e5747fe09aab443be3e97b9b901002e2a1251, parent ff5d8913c666578a438d7e6a032843c1531af3a4) has an empty description and no closes_issues entry, and gnome-text-editor MR 206 'editor-window: Always show a confirmation dialog when discarding changes' (5a293da8b68c169a6d020e1a1509e6fd2742c65a, parent b71c5e4f2e7eccacced8205926e83e971cdc7315) describes the bug in prose but links no issue. Both shas were verified to exist and are reachable from the default branch, so either can be promoted if the gate later accepts a merge request as the sole authority

candidateDefects is null for nine pool entries because no defect mining was run against them. Where a count is present it is a stated metric, not a qualified defect list: for the three GNOME projects it is the number of merged merge requests among the most recent 100 whose description closes or fixes a numbered issue, and for rnote it is the GitHub search count of merged pull requests linked to an issue. None of those counts has been filtered for offline runnability or observability

verification.method: GitLab REST API v4 for gitlab.gnome.org projects and the authenticated gh CLI for github.com, plus blobless clones of gnome-calculator, gnome-text-editor, gnome-clocks, and rnote
verification.shaCheck: every affectedRevision and fixedRevision was confirmed with git cat-file -t (all report 'commit') and with git merge-base --is-ancestor against origin/HEAD (all reachable from the default branch)
verification.toolkitCheck: GTK linkage was read from the build manifest at each affected revision, not at HEAD and not per repository, and the proving line is quoted in each toolkitEvidence entry
verification.issueCheck: issue titles came from the API (closes_issues for GNOME merge requests, the issues endpoint for rnote). GNOME's API returns the newer /-/work_items/<n> form; the canonical /-/issues/<n> URLs recorded here were each confirmed to return HTTP 200
